authentication.credential_handling: See the companion safety_policy artifact. The token value must be read directly from the file at request time and must never be echoed, logged, written into any result artifact, embedded in a committed script, or included in a typed status update.

schemes.note: BV-BRC user identity token. This deployment treats a bearer BV-BRC identity as the caller identity for owner-scoped and workspace-backed operations.
Service-account style credential mapped to an API-key tenant.

deployment.note: Only asm-next is in scope for this work.

documented_bounds_and_gotchas.bound: 1 to 500, default 100; paginate with the opaque cursor echoed in the X-Next-Cursor response header, which is absent on the last page
more than max_chunk_ids entries returns 422 rather than truncating; discover the actual limit empirically or from /v1/config

documented_bounds_and_gotchas.gotcha: GET /v1/documents and DELETE /v1/documents/{doc_id} cannot name a collection and silently target the caller's effective default. Never infer a named collection's document inventory from /v1/documents.
Graph endpoints degrade to available=false with null counts instead of erroring. An empty graph result is indistinguishable from an unconfigured graph store unless /v1/graph/stats is checked first.
GET /v1/stats/tenants with counts=true probes every (tenant, collection, store) cell and can take seconds on a large deployment. Poll no faster than roughly every 15 seconds.

If no LLM endpoint is configured for the tenant, /v1/query returns a retrieval-only placeholder rather than failing. A scorer that does not detect this will record a configuration as catastrophically bad when it was never actually generating.
Treat a truthy truncated flag as a distinct outcome class in the scorer, not as a wrong answer.

429 with Retry-After is used for in-flight guards; 503 is used for fail-closed store outages. Both are transient and must be retried with backoff and recorded as errors in the cost vector, never scored as answer failures.

grading_subsystem_reference.read_only_probe: GET /v1/grading/batches answers 200 with an empty list for a caller with no reads, and 404 on a server that does not implement grading.
grading_subsystem_reference.status: present on this tenant but OUT OF SCOPE as a mutation surface
grading_subsystem_reference.structure: A batch carries a rubric hash, a seed, and named readers; each task pairs a question with a document and evidence sets of spans; readers submit independent verdicts and an admin adjudicates. Batch creation is admin-only.
grading_subsystem_reference.why_recorded: Its verdict vocabulary is the deployment's own native notion of answer quality and is the recommended basis for the offline scorer's failure taxonomy.

read_only_in_scope.use: Enumerate the ASM paper collections this token can read. Also reports the caller's effective default collection, which is the same resolution /v1/query, /v1/retrieve and /v1/chunks use when `collection` is omitted. This is the authoritative discovery step for 'the different ASM papers collections'.
Declarations only: template id, version, hash, label, output shape, columns, slots. The system/user bodies are deliberately never returned. This enumerates the prompt-template axis of the sweep.
Models assignable per-request to the hot-swappable llm and reranker tasks. Enumerates the model axis. base_urls are not exposed.
Retrieval without generation. Isolates retrieval quality from generation quality; use it to score recall of gold chunks independently of the answer text.

Full RAG flow: optional query rewrite (HyDE / multi-query), hybrid retrieval per variant, RRF fusion, optional cross-encoder rerank, grounded generation. Per-request llm and reranker overrides swap those clients for that request only, leaving the global assignment and the corpus fixed, which the API documents as a clean A/B.

Fetch chunks by id, typically the prev_chunk_id / next_chunk_id carried in a Source's metadata, to expand neighbouring context. Also the mechanism for resolving a cited chunk_id back to its text when verifying a citation. Exceeding max_chunk_ids is a 422, never a silent truncation.

List indexed documents with document-level metadata (title, doc_type, doi, chunk_count). IMPLICIT-collection only: there is no per-collection documents endpoint, so it targets whatever an omitted `collection` resolves to for this caller.
Entity and relationship counts. Degrades to available=false with null counts when no graph store is configured; check this before designing any graph-dependent structure.
Entities most-connected first. Seed set for graph-guided query expansion.
Per-store vector/text/graph counts summed over readable collections.

Caller identity, readable tenants, collection allowlist, per-(tenant,collection) counts. Call with counts=false for the cheap identity-only answer; counts=true probes every store and can take seconds.
Server configuration as exposed to callers.
Liveness and build identity. /v1/version reports package version, git tag, git sha, start time.

candidates.description: One POST /v1/query per benchmark question. The control arm every other structure must beat.

candidates.cost_shape: n+1 generation calls, n+1 retrieval passes
candidates.description: Answer, then judge the answer against the question for sufficiency and enumerate gaps, then issue gap-targeted follow-up queries and re-answer. Mirrors strategy.assess_answer and strategy.followup_queries in the reference.
candidates.reference_detail: The reference sends the candidate answer to the assessor whole and unabridged, on the stated grounds that sufficiency is a property of the whole answer and a judgement made from a truncated answer is a judgement of a different object. It returns {sufficient, confidence, gaps[], rationale} and is deliberately strict: a hedged answer is not sufficient.

candidates.description: Split the question into sub-questions, retrieve and answer each independently, then synthesize with the sub-answers and their citations as context.

Seed from GET /v1/graph/entities, expand with GET /v1/graph/neighbors/{entity} at depth 1-2, use the resulting entity and predicate vocabulary as query expansion, then query. Inert unless graph stats report available.

Retrieve with context_window=0, then selectively expand only the top-scoring sources through GET /v1/chunks using their prev_chunk_id / next_chunk_id, then generate. A cheaper targeted alternative to raising context_window globally.

candidates.applicability: Only for benchmark questions that are genuinely enumerative; misapplied to a single-fact question it is pure overhead.
candidates.description: Treat the answer as a set of required cells rather than prose. Maintain a durable frontier of unfilled cells, search to fill missing rows, and stop when count targets are covered. The reference's table_fill mode.

For a given deficit, generate sibling prompt arms that each mutate exactly one thing -- expected source shape, external terminology, anchoring breadth, or context-qualifier emphasis -- so the contrast between siblings is attributable. The reference enforces one delta per arm and shares seed vocabulary across all arms of a call so seeds cannot differentially bias one sibling against another.

credit_and_cost_discipline_from_referenc.bound_vs_convergence: A run cut by a declared resource bound must be recorded as bound_hit and must never be reported as convergence.
credit_and_cost_discipline_from_referenc.cost_vector: Cost is recorded as a vector, not a scalar: provider_calls, llm_calls, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, returned_hits, fetched_bytes, retries, wall_ms, errors. billable_calls = provider_calls + llm_calls is the one place two units are summed, defensible because both count discrete paid round trips.
credit_and_cost_discipline_from_referenc.credit_rule: Credit is assigned once, after accepted evidence has been written into typed state, and only for a logical slot that is new to that state. A repeat assignment onto an already-filled slot is recorded as uncredited volume, not as yield.
credit_and_cost_discipline_from_referenc.relevance_here: This is the natural shape for comparing episode structures. An iterative structure that lifts the correctness rate by three points at four times the call cost is a different verdict from one that lifts it for free, and a scalar score hides that.
credit_and_cost_discipline_from_referenc.yield_rule: score = credited datapoints per billable call. When no cost record exists the score is null, never the raw datapoint count -- a yield that has not been divided by anything must not be read as a yield.

episode_structure_axes.note: These are candidate workflow shapes for the repeated unit, drawn from the reference implementation at github.com/chian/nano-graphrag/tree/main/question_pipeline. They are structures to compare, not a prescribed design.

generation.values: enumerate from GET /v1/prompt-templates; record id, version and hash with every trial
enumerate from GET /v1/models/available where task is llm

generation.status: exact request field names unverified; resolve from QueryRequest before use

parameter_search_space.note: Axes are independent unless a dependency is stated. Full cross-product is large; the workflow is expected to move one axis at a time from a declared baseline and record the delta, not to enumerate.

retrieval.hypothesis: bm25 should win on exact strain names, gene symbols, accession numbers and table captions; vector should win on paraphrased conceptual questions; hybrid should dominate on a mixed set.
Larger top_k raises recall and raises distractor load; the interaction with rerank is the interesting effect, not the main effect.

retrieval.values: enumerate from GET /v1/models/available where task is reranker

retrieval.hypothesis: Helps questions whose answer straddles a chunk boundary; costs prompt budget on everything else.

retrieval.precondition: GET /v1/graph/stats reports available=true with non-zero counts; otherwise this axis is inert and must be recorded as not-tested rather than as no-effect.

retrieval.hypothesis: Per-collection scoping reduces cross-collection distractors; the union raises recall for questions whose evidence is split. Because Source.collection is stamped only on multi-collection requests, the union arm additionally yields per-collection attribution for free.
values: the multi-collection union, up to the 5-collection maximum

provenance.trust: UNTRUSTED external data. Treat every field below as a starting hypothesis. The executing Episode MUST re-fetch /ragstack/asm-next/api/openapi.json and reconcile before relying on any parameter name or bound.

QueryRequest.REQUIRED_FIRST_ACTION: The executing Episode must GET /ragstack/asm-next/api/openapi.json, resolve #/components/schemas/QueryRequest in full, and write the resolved schema into the run's own evidence directory before sweeping any parameter. Do not guess field names from this artifact.
known_from_endpoint_description: query rewriting is available in HyDE and multi-query forms
hybrid retrieval runs per rewritten variant and results are fused with RRF
a per-request `llm` override swaps the generation client for that request only
a per-request `reranker` override swaps the rerank client for that request only
a prompt `template` is selectable from the declarations returned by GET /v1/prompt-templates
when no LLM endpoint is configured the answer is a retrieval-only placeholder
QueryRequest.status: NOT CAPTURED. The full field list sits in a region of openapi.json the Duet's read-only fetch truncated.

collection.note: omitted resolves to the caller's effective default

collections.note: multi-collection request; stamps Source.collection on each result

QueryResponse.serialization_note: Provenance fields are omitted rather than emitted as null, so absence is normal and must not be read as an error.

Source.collection: string; stamped only on a multi-collection request, otherwise omitted
Source.context: ContextChunk[]; present only when context_window > 0, otherwise omitted
Source.metadata: object; carries document fields plus prev_chunk_id / next_chunk_id (null at document boundaries)
